$comment: One owner per defect class: detector → owner (the lens or agent whose finding it is) → fixer → fallback when the owner's pack is not installed → home pack. Today's agent names are used; `target` names the Phase-6 consolidated role (proposal §3.5) so the merge has a map. An agent's Boundary section should agree with this file: if two agents both claim a class here, one of them is wrong. JSON for the same reason as thresholds.json (stdlib consumers). Edit a row, never fork a class into two rows.

n-plus-one.fallback: the database detector's own report when performance is not installed
n-plus-one.note: query-optimizer's knowledge is fix guidance for this class, not a second detector

wcag.detector: frontend/skills/a11y-code-scan (source) · frontend/skills/a11y-scan (axe at route-state; THR-A11Y.axe_gate, gate G9) · mobile/skills/mobile-a11y-scan (native)
wcag.owner: ui-ux/agents/ux-reviewer (the one WCAG judge, web and native)
wcag.fixer: /frontend-fix (frontend) · /mobile-fix (mobile); contrast, focus ring and tap target through ui-design-sweep verbs 12, 13 and 16 (/polish, /enhance-ui); the implementer applies
wcag.fallback: frontend/agents/accessibility-auditor when ui-ux is not installed; native screens: the verifier judges mobile-a11y-scan's rows
wcag.note: one class, three detectors: mobile-a11y is the native half of this row, not a second owner

workflow-transitions.detector: backend/skills/state-transition-scan §1–§2 (FSM-library semantics: an illegal event answered as success, a terminal state re-opened)

engine-tuning.fixer: operator, behind an ADR for durability settings

acceptance-verdict.fixer: implementer (SPEC_CONFLICT when the contract is wrong)

ui-states.detector: ui-ux/skills/ui-state-scan · ui-ux/skills/state-matrix (state-matrix-lint.py, gate G12 state-matrix; vocabulary THR-UI-STATES)
ui-states.fixer: /frontend-fix · /mobile-fix (the missing branch, failing first); the visual treatment through ui-design-sweep verbs 9–11 (/polish, /enhance-ui)
ui-states.fallback: UNREVIEWED(states) — ux-reviewer not installed (ui-ux pack); the lint still runs when the skill is installed
ui-states.note: the matrix is written at P3 by ui-ux/agents/ux-designer (design.md UI slice by the architect without it)

client-data.fixer: /frontend-fix; a server-side cause → /db-fix or /perf-fix; a cross-user cache leak → /security-fix
client-data.fallback: client-data-scan's own report, verified by the verifier
client-data.note: owns optimistic rollback (CD-05) and UI request races across renders (§3); code-quality correctness-smell-scan §3 keeps the single-effect case

routing.fixer: /frontend-fix (a path, param, redirect target or public status code is a stop-and-ask change)
routing.fallback: routing-scan's own report, verified by the verifier
routing.note: navigation-speed keeps hard reloads and scroll restoration; a11y-code-scan keeps route-change focus

i18n-completeness.fixer: /frontend-fix (non-source locales are the translators' call — stop and ask)
i18n-completeness.fallback: i18n-scan's own report, verified by the verifier
i18n-completeness.note: /i18n-audit is /frontend-audit --classes=i18n; correctness-smell-scan §6 keeps clock and zone arithmetic, i18n-scan §4 the presentation formatting

seo.fixer: /frontend-fix (SEO row); a canonical or public status change is stop-and-ask
seo.fallback: seo-audit's own report, verified by the verifier

design-tokens.fixer: by remedy: ui-design-sweep verbs 1–2 (/polish, /enhance-ui) · /align once the token exists · /unify-surfaces for a wrapper
design-tokens.fallback: design-token-audit's own report; ui-reviewer detects and routes

chart-encoding.fixer: the implementer at the chart; a data ramp as tokens → ui-ux/agents/design-system-architect

mobile-lifecycle.note: durability of queued writes is offline-sync's; a purpose string that changes the store answer is store-compliance's

mobile-perf.detector: mobile/skills/mobile-perf-scan (existence) · mobile/skills/device-harness (cost on a named device)
mobile-perf.owner: mobile/agents/device-performance-auditor (judge; runs mobile-perf-scan and device-harness itself, measures and ranks)
mobile-perf.fixer: /mobile-fix; the cost proof is re-measured by device-performance-auditor
mobile-perf.fallback: the verifier judges mobile-perf-scan's rows; cost: not measured

mobile-a11y.fallback: repo-baseline/.claude/agents/verifier when ui-ux is not installed
mobile-a11y.note: the native half of wcag (same owner); platform-conventions-audit keeps platform conventions only

offline-sync.fallback: offline-sync-scan's own report, durability capped at unproven

store-compliance.fixer: /mobile-fix (config and code); wording, metadata and review notes stay with the human

app-size.owner: mobile/agents/device-performance-auditor (cold start as the measured cost)
app-size.note: store size limits are store-compliance-scan's table, cited not restated

native-bridge.owner: repo-baseline/.claude/agents/verifier (judges /mobile-audit's Native bridge row); whether a bridge should exist → mobile/agents/mobile-architect

mobile-security.fixer: /security-fix (mobile row); a shipped server secret is rotated first
mobile-security.note: /mobile-audit's Device security row consumes it when the security pack is installed

obs-logs.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-logs.note: dropped or swallowed error → code-quality error-handling-scan; a sensitive value or redaction gap → security data-exposure-scan § 6; log injection → security injection-scan; volume cost → finops

obs-correlation.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-correlation.note: proxy and ingress access-log format → infrastructure

obs-tracing.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-tracing.note: coverage target → distributed-systems; observability owns the propagation mechanics and the telemetry flush inside the shutdown chain (devops owns the chain)

obs-sampling.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-sampling.note: a sampling-rate change is stop-and-ask in /obs-fix; cost → finops

obs-metrics.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-metrics.note: cost → finops (observability carries the series arithmetic, THR-OBS-CARDINALITY)

obs-health.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-health.note: liveness on a shared dependency → performance request-path-scan §15; probe presence and shape in manifests → infrastructure k8s-availability-scan §2; public health details → security data-exposure-scan § 3

obs-error-tracking.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-error-tracking.note: publicly served source maps → security xss-scan § 13; sendDefaultPii / dataCollection → security; native symbol upload (dSYM, R8 mapping) → mobile

obs-alert-rules.fallback: alert-rule-lint's own report; behaviour (dead, noisy, flapping) → observability/skills/alert-audit, NO-DATA without fire history
obs-alert-rules.note: alert-audit keeps the behavioural half and consumes alert-rule-lint's rows; PrometheusRule schema → infrastructure; a neutered CI rules gate → devops

obs-routing.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-routing.note: AM and notification secrets inline → security secret-scan; who gets paged is stop-and-ask in /obs-fix

obs-slo.fallback: slo-rule-scan's own report; attainment → observability/skills/slo-audit, NO-DATA without a backend
obs-slo.note: slo-audit owns attainment and is the single writer of ai/runtime/slos.md; /alert-design proposes rows and dispatches it; burn arithmetic is THR-OBS-BURN

obs-pipeline.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
obs-pipeline.note: collector RBAC: breadth → security iac-scan §3; missing or dangling (SA, roleRef, a needed verb) → infrastructure k8s-wiring-scan §6 (observability reports the telemetry blast radius as corroboration)

ci-pipeline-integrity.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
ci-pipeline-integrity.note: test-job mask, zero tests and test retries → testing suite-execution-scan §4/§6; lint-job mask → code-quality suppression-scan; a11y gate → frontend a11y-scan §7; devops supplies the required-check join (ci-graph.py --required) those owners read for severity

ci-cache.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
ci-cache.note: cache poisoning (a PR-writable cache read by release) → security ci-security-scan §5

release-integrity.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
release-integrity.note: registry tag-mutability → security iac-scan 4j (registry variant); retention/rollback → devops DP-9; deploy by mutable tag → security iac-scan 4j (release §4/§7 corroborate); revisionHistoryLimit → infrastructure

deploy-safety.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
deploy-safety.note: migration statements → database migration-safety / migration-rehearsal; probes → performance request-path-scan §15, observability HC-01, infrastructure K-PROBE-*; preStop and grace timings → infrastructure (THR-SHUTDOWN-GRACE)

env-parity.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier

container-build.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
container-build.note: final stage as root, secret ARG/ENV, secret files, ADD URL / curl|sh, TLS verification disabled → security iac-scan §1 (container-build-scan supplies the stage-chain awk)

compose-reliability.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
compose-reliability.note: ports, privilege, docker socket, default passwords → security iac-scan §2

progressive-delivery.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
progressive-delivery.note: AnalysisTemplate selector grounding → observability rule-inventory.py --check=selectors (when installed; else report-flagged)

gitops-reconciliation.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier
gitops-reconciliation.note: controller spec (prune, waves, selfHeal × HPA, ignoreDifferences) → infrastructure; plaintext kind: Secret in git → security

ci-supply-chain.note: every CI attacker-path class on all six platforms (injection, privileged triggers, pinning × privilege, cache poisoning, OIDC width, secret exposure, runner trust); pin × privilege is graded with ci-graph.py --check=pin-priv; without the security pack, devops pipeline-integrity-scan runs the greps and tags rows security-class (owner pack not installed)

iac-state.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
iac-state.note: secret values in state → security secret-scan (iac-state-scan §2 corroborates the mechanism: ephemeral, write-only, state encryption); PIN-HELM covers charts installed by runbooks, CI and Argo/Flux

iac-lifecycle.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
iac-lifecycle.note: infrastructure/skills/tf-plan-review is the plan-time verdict over §4 on a saved plan; IAM and security-group widening in a plan → security iac-scan

deletion-safety.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
deletion-safety.note: destroy-surviving backups → infrastructure dr-audit §12 corroborates; one class across TF, CFN/SAM, CDK, Pulumi and K8s PV/StorageClass (THR-KMS-WINDOW)

data-durability.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
data-durability.note: backup exposure chain (a public policy over the backup prefix) → security iac-scan §4; DB TLS not enforced (DATA-06) → security; recoverability (backups in the app's bucket, writer can delete) stays here; THR-BACKUP-DRILL-AGE, THR-BACKUP-RETENTION

serverless-reliability.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
serverless-reliability.note: log retention (SLS-07) → infrastructure iac-cost; unbounded scale on a finite downstream is credited here (SLS-05), cost corroborates; THR-QUEUE-VISIBILITY

iac-cost.owner: infrastructure/agents/infra-reviewer (judge, refute mode) for existence · finops/agents/cost-reviewer (diff) / finops/agents/finops-analyst (bill) for price
iac-cost.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
iac-cost.note: candidates carry quantity × unit (price key), never a $ without a bill line or a dated pricing page; fallback for pricing: infrastructure /cost-audit, which consumes the candidates and never re-detects an IaC class; THR-SCALE-CEILING

k8s-render.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
k8s-render.note: live reconciliation drift → devops gitops-audit; the render contract (§0) is the shared input of the four k8s detectors

k8s-availability.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
k8s-availability.note: liveness on a dependency → performance request-path-scan §15; shutdown code and image chain → devops deploy-safety-scan §5 / container-build-scan §2 (THR-SHUTDOWN-GRACE is owned here); CPU limits are precedents/infrastructure.md § 1, not a class; THR-K8S-PROD-FLOOR

k8s-wiring.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
k8s-wiring.note: RBAC privilege breadth → security iac-scan §3; RBAC wiring (missing SA, dangling roleRef or subject, a missing needed verb, automount off on an API caller) stays here (§6); NetworkPolicy width → security iac-scan 4k

k8s-api-schema.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
k8s-api-schema.note: PromQL content → observability alert-rule-lint; weak PSA enforce level → security (an enforce level that rejects the namespace's own workloads stays here, §3)

edge-reliability.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
edge-reliability.note: cross-user cache (E4) → security iac-scan §6 (§4 here is the tagged fallback); log content → security data-exposure-scan §6; shipper and retention of self-hosted backends → observability telemetry-config-scan; access-log format and request id (E21) stay here (§15)

dns-tls-lifecycle.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
dns-tls-lifecycle.note: §1 owns D2 TTL and the record target lifecycle (an address a deletable object owns, copied where you cannot edit it: D1's non-claimable half); dangling DNS / takeover → security (§7 here is the tagged fallback); alert-rule quality → observability alert-rule-lint; THR-CERT-EXPIRY-ALERT, THR-DNS-CUTOVER-TTL

network-correctness.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode (verifier.md); without it a Task refuter
network-correctness.note: classes here: N3 NACL return path, N-PEER-ROUTE, NAT zone affinity and path MTU/ICMP (§1), N7 CIDR overlap (§2), N8 IPv6 connectivity and N-PRIVDNS private resolution (§3), declared-vs-running drift (§4); §5 live exposure rows → security (executor lane, rows carry owner: security); declared exposure, egress-all (N2) and ipBlock width → security iac-scan; SG cidr_blocks and ipBlock are references, never allocations (precedents/infrastructure.md § 67)

shared-cache-leak.fallback: infrastructure/skills/edge-reliability-scan §4 runs the greps when security is not installed, rows tagged security-class (owner pack not installed)
shared-cache-leak.note: a shared cache serving one user's response to another (E4); the two-identity probe is an exploit-payloads.md row; consistent with frontend's cross-user cache rule and tenant-leak

dangling-dns.fallback: infrastructure/skills/dns-tls-lifecycle-scan §7 runs the greps when security is not installed, rows tagged security-class (owner pack not installed)
dangling-dns.note: D1 takeover: credited to security when the target is claimable; a dangling record that only breaks resolution (released EIP, deleted zone) is infrastructure dns-tls-lifecycle-scan §1-adjacent; a literal CNAME to CloudFront or an ELB is not a takeover (precedents/infrastructure.md § 39)

messaging-delivery.fallback: performance/skills/request-path-scan §24 runs its greps for consumer idempotency, poison/DLQ and lock or visibility vs run time when distributed-systems is not installed; with it installed §24 prints → messaging-scan §2/§3/§6 and does not grade
messaging-delivery.note: one oracle for the shared half: V296 is perf V44 probe 1; money, stock and credit effects → security logic-race-scan §4–§5; Lambda and EventBridge event sources → infrastructure serverless-reliability-scan §2–§4 (THR-QUEUE-VISIBILITY); worker concurrency, prefetch numbers and partitions vs consumers → performance request-path-scan §23; publish inside an open transaction → database transaction-scan §1; THR-DS-CONSUMER-TIMING

dual-write.fallback: the detector's own report, tagged, when the judge is not run; publish or enqueue inside an open transaction stays database transaction-scan §1 whether or not this pack is installed
dual-write.note: publish or enqueue INSIDE a transaction is database transaction-scan §1 (V8); the outbox writer outside the caller's transaction is §1 here and database transaction-scan §2 corroborates; the relay's claim without SKIP LOCKED is database transaction-scan §5; a consumer with no reserve is messaging-scan §2; money effects → security logic-race-scan §4–§5; THR-DS-DEDUPE-WINDOW

retry-policy.fallback: backend outbound-client rows, tagged retry-policy (owner pack not installed)
retry-policy.note: timeout presence → performance request-path-scan §12; proxy and load-balancer retries → infrastructure edge-reliability-scan §3; serverless retries → infrastructure serverless-reliability-scan §6; a retried charge or a provider key minted per attempt → security logic-race-scan §4; a message that keeps failing → messaging-scan §3; Temporal activity options → workflow-scan §3; THR-RES-RETRY (layers: 1)

distributed-lock.owner: distributed-systems/agents/resilience-reviewer (judge, refute mode; locks and leases) · distributed-systems/agents/system-architect (leader rows, §6)
distributed-lock.fallback: performance/skills/request-path-scan §18 for the per-replica and fencing half when distributed-systems is not installed
distributed-lock.note: a lock held per replica and a correctness lease with no fencing token stay performance request-path-scan §18 (V38) — §4 here supplies the 4d fencing grep and the lease arithmetic; once-per-fleet schedulers stay performance §20 (V40); migrations at boot → devops deploy-safety-scan §1 (the runner table is precedents/performance.md § 77); the pooler setting → database connection-config-scan §3; a queue job outliving its broker lock → messaging-scan §6; THR-DS-LEASE

clock-misuse.note: token exp/iat units and leeway → security (@auth-reviewer); client last-write-wins → mobile offline-sync-scan §4; a single process's schedule zone and self-overlap → backend job-lifecycle-scan §6 and §4 (§11 here owns the coordinated half); events ordered by created_at across streams are §9 here (event-contract-scan hands them over)

workflow-determinism.note: activity configuration (retries, timeouts, heartbeats) is §3 here, and the activity is one layer of retry-deadline-scan §4; saga isolation (lost update) → database transaction-scan §8; money compensations → security logic-race-scan §4; job payload drift inside one service → backend job-lifecycle-scan §3; Step Functions Task TimeoutSeconds/HeartbeatSeconds stay §3 here

event-contract.detector: distributed-systems/skills/event-contract-scan §1–§10 (buf, json-schema-diff, asyncapi, oasdiff for webhooks, the avsc resolver)
event-contract.fallback: testing/skills/contract-test for consumer-driven contracts (Pact message pacts)
event-contract.note: split at the boundary: a parsed message cast to a type with no runtime check is code-quality type-safety-scan §1 (§2 here owns the contract half: a schema'd topic read without its deserializer, and what a malformed event does to the consumer); HTTP API spec drift → backend http-contract-scan §10 (oasdiff here only on webhooks this service sends); job payload drift inside one service → backend job-lifecycle-scan §3; money as a float in a payload → backend wire-format-scan §5; ORDER BY created_at across streams → coordination-scan §9; a per-replica projection daemon → performance request-path-scan §20

api-contract.detector: backend/skills/http-contract-scan §1–§13 (dto-types.py for the body-type and status columns)
api-contract.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode
api-contract.note: BA-10 on money, credit, order, paid-send and webhook routes → security logic-race-scan §4; consistency across sibling endpoints → backend api-consistency-audit; webhook contracts this service sends → distributed-systems event-contract-scan

input-validation.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode
input-validation.note: operator objects and mass assignment → security injection-scan; BO-03 outbound casts → code-quality type-safety-scan §1; @Type(() => Date) and other time binding → backend wire-format-scan §6

edge-errors.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode
edge-errors.note: error body content → security data-exposure-scan §1/§2; a local catch → code-quality error-handling-scan §6; the error envelope's shape → THR-ERR-ENVELOPE

wire-format.detector: backend/skills/wire-format-scan §1–§8 (§8 the clock seam is an enabler, never a finding)
wire-format.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode
wire-format.note: arithmetic and the clock in code → code-quality correctness-smell-scan §4/§6; money as a float in an event payload is §5 here; THR-MONEY.wire

job-lifecycle.fallback: the detector's own report, verified by the verifier in refute mode
job-lifecycle.note: in-transaction enqueue → database transaction-scan §1; consumer idempotency, retry eligibility, poison/DLQ → distributed-systems messaging-scan; coordinated schedules across replicas → distributed-systems coordination-scan §11; once-per-fleet → performance request-path-scan §20
